headline: FTC Launches Curtain Conspiracy Probe Amid Humming Compliance Failures
deck: EU Opacity Tariffs Spark Trade War Over Fabric Regulations and Polite Entry Protocols
article:
The Federal Trade Commission opened a sweeping inquiry into European Union curtain opacity tariffs after American textile companies logged repeated humming compliance shortfalls. FTC Spokesperson Al Woven calibrated his enter-humming meter and declared the agency would enforce minimum opacity standards from international pacts.

Agency logs recorded 312 fabric-rustling episodes during closed-curtain hearings, each breaching the precise decibel bands required for polite entry. Woven stressed the need to uphold social contracts and waved away suggestions that fabric tweaks alone could erode national privacy benchmarks.

A fresh tariff chart lists exact decibel allowances tied to fabric weight. An internal memo noted 14-day blackout-curtain delays have stalled 47 federal lobbies and slowed legislation continent-wide. Local curtain hobbyist Mildred T. Veil called the lapses a direct threat to humming rituals and household seclusion.

Analysts warn that sustained violations may produce a fabric-free trade corridor, shredding cross-border etiquette and stalling curtain diplomacy. Harmony in humming remains the last thread holding intercontinental manners together.
author: Clara T. Drape, Senior Bureaucratic Correspondent

oped.title: Curtains for the Regulators: Why the FTC's Probe Is Just Sour Humming
oped.author: Lord Alistair Drapeworth, Emeritus Professor of Veil Supremacy at the Institute for Uninvited Entry
oped.body: The FTC's curtain probe is fabric-phobia masquerading as oversight. Privacy in 2026 rests on synchronized humming, not obsolete door barriers. The true culprits are EU tariffs that punish importers of whisper-thin voile seeking market share. Compliance shortfalls trace to wide-brimmed hats that muffle entry vibrations and compel clumsy throat-clearing. The remedy is state humming licenses with mandatory falsetto for outsiders. If a handful of curtain twitchers forfeit their right to lurk behind brocade, margins may finally recover.

stories.headline: US Fabric Exporters Face 18% Tariff After EU Classifies Standard Curtains as Opaque
stories.deck: Midwest mills now pivot to sheer imports while Congress debates thread-count subsidies.
stories.article:
The EU opacity tariff has shuttered two North Carolina mills; every standard-weave batch now draws the surcharge absent laboratory-certified translucence. Brussels-bound shipments must carry notarized humming logs at every checkpoint.

Threadwise Industries executives are pressing for federal fabric credits after a 37 percent order drop and looming beige shortages for suburban restocking.

stories.headline: Suburban Burglar Convicted After Using Delivery Hums to Access Seven Homes
stories.deck: Prosecutors noted the suspect's four-note sequence matched local pizza drivers exactly.
stories.article:
A Loudoun County jury convicted Daniel Pruitt on 14 counts after recordings proved he had replicated the three-second hum of neighborhood delivery workers. He entered homes at dusk, lifted only electronics, and left curtains undisturbed to dodge neighbor scrutiny.

Defense counsel claimed the sequence was common property, yet the court held that commercial reuse of the threshold signal violated polite-entry statutes.

stories.headline: HOA Votes to Fine Residents Whose Curtains Fail Quarterly Opacity Inspection
stories.deck: The new rule requires monthly fabric swatches submitted alongside HOA dues.
stories.article:
Willow Creek homeowners approved fines after complaints that sheer panels let streetlight spill into living rooms after dark. Inspectors will now carry light meters and levy $75 penalties on any panel passing more than 12 percent illumination.

Board president Harold Finch framed the rule as a clarification of the privacy contract, with noncompliant homes offered vouchers for approved local fabric only.
